yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every detail survives, with useful glosses: "One tag covers a tree up to 5 inches (13 cm) across and 10 feet (3 m) tall", "Fourth graders (Year 4 kids)", "(note: a $2.50 service fee will still apply)".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "up for grabs", "does the forest's health a favour", "feed for wildlife" for forage.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, plain Australian notice English: "Get in touch with us for current hours.", "have a careful read". "Chrissy tree permits" sits oddly beside "Christmas Tree permit" in the next heading.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light touch, right for level 2: "Chrissy tree", "up for grabs", "have a careful read", "does the forest's health a favour". No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Stays an informative public notice, lightly warmed: "priority goes to people who can't cut their own tree."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "Taking them out of the designated areas helps the other trees grow bigger and can open up areas with feed for wildlife."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Some variety but light: "up for grabs", "Chrissy" twice, "does ... a favour".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the permit notice: "The SFNF's Christmas tree permits are $10 and non-refundable."

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts survive, but with added framing and claims: "Here's one for ya. If you fancy chopping down your own Chrissy tree this year", "Everyone's a winner.", and "Give them a bell" turns the forest service's "Contact us" into a third party.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fitting ("first dibs", "set you back $10"), but "they'll sting you an extra $2.50" casts a service fee as a rip-off, and "patches of bush" is fine.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Some natural lines ("will set you back $10", "Give them a bell"), but stock phrases are bolted on: "Here's one for ya.", "packed in like sardines", "wouldn't you know it", "Everyone's a winner."
yarn-troppo.register: Far heavier than level 2: a pub-yarn opener "Here's one for ya.", "take the axe to", "whopper", "sting you", "packed in like sardines". Closer to level 4. No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: A neutral public notice turned jokey and a little cynical: "Buy one online through recreation.gov and they'll sting you an extra $2.50 service fee on top."
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively, with some forced joins: "Saturdays only, mind,", "So a 15-foot (4.6 m) whopper? That's two tags."
yarn-troppo.variety: Widely varied: "up for grabs", "first dibs", "Give them a bell", "set you back", "whopper", "a power of good".
yarn-troppo.essence: The facts are there, but the notice becomes a chatty pitch: "And here's the good bit".

dinkum-3.meaning: Every detail is kept: "people who can't cut their own tree get first dibs", "so a 15-foot (4.6 m) tree, say, needs two".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "first dibs", "pop in the pass or voucher number", "heads up", "does the bush a good turn".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural on the whole, but "Chrissie tree" is leaned on so hard in an official notice that it starts to sound put on: "The SFNF's Chrissie tree permits are $10".
dinkum-3.register: About right for level 2: "Chrissie", "first dibs", "pop in", "heads up", "skinny little trees". No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Stays an informative notice, warmly: "Make sure you have a proper read of the overview".
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth, but the repeated "Chrissie tree" grates: "the trees there tend to be just the right size for a Chrissie tree."
dinkum-3.variety: "Chrissie tree" appears seven times; the rest is varied ("first dibs", "heads up", "pop in").
dinkum-3.essence: Clearly the notice: "Year 4 kids with an Every Kid Outdoors pass can get a Chrissie tree permit for free".

engine.meaning: The original almost verbatim, so the facts survive: "The SFNF’s non-refundable Christmas tree permits are $10."
engine.sense: Mechanical swaps miss: "Local bush health experts" turns forest-health specialists into something like bush-medicine experts, and "improves bush health" strains.
engine.authenticity: Untouched US notice English with swaps bolted on: "Cutting a Chrissy tree also improves bush health.", "Fourth graders with Every Kid Outdoors pass are eligible".
engine.register: Largely untranslated: only "Chrissy" and "bush" change. Well short of level 2.
engine.tone: The neutral notice tone survives because the text does: "It is important to carefully read the overview".
engine.flow: Reads as the original, but "Local bush health experts identify areas" is a jarring join.
engine.essence: It is the original notice: "Pre-cut Christmas Trees may be available for purchase at district offices."

unharnessed.meaning: Every detail is kept: "(note: a $2.50 service fee will be charged)", "a 15-foot tree needs two tags".
unharnessed.sense: The few terms fit: "up for grabs", "first dibs going to people who can't cut their own tree".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain English, but US forms are left: "Fourth graders with an Every Kid Outdoors pass", imperial units only.
unharnessed.register: Lighter than level 2: beyond plainer wording, only "up for grabs" and "first dibs".
unharnessed.tone: Stays an informative public notice: "It's important to read the overview and need-to-know information carefully".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Taking these trees out of designated areas helps the other trees grow bigger".
unharnessed.variety: Little slang to vary: "up for grabs", "first dibs".
